raw_response:
I farm 12 mu in Quzhou — our soil is decent loam but getting a bit tired after so many years of double cropping. I read the county extension pamphlets and talk to the input dealer in town, so I try to balance NPK rather than just dumping urea like some neighbors do. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kg/mu and maize about 600 kg/mu, so I will keep roughly the same plan but trim nitrogen slightly — urea went up again this spring and I can see no yield gain from pushing past 22-23 kg N on wheat.

For winter wheat, I will sow improved semi-dwarf varieties like Jimai 22 in early October, about 15 kg seed per mu. I will put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base at two bags per mu, then topdress urea at jointing. Total N around 22 kg/mu, P2O5 about 9 kg, K2O about 7. I irrigate four times — before winter, jointing, heading, grain filling — since well water is available but electricity costs something. Pesticide: one herbicide in spring, one for aphids/powdery mildew, sometimes a third at heading for fusarium if it rains.

For summer maize, I direct-seed a hybrid like Zhengdan 958 or Denghai right after wheat harvest, no-till to save time and moisture. N around 20 kg/mu split between seeding and big-trumpet stage, lighter P and K since wheat residue returns some. Summer rains usually cover water needs — one irrigation if July is dry. Two pesticide rounds: corn borer and armyworm.

Tillage: I plough before wheat every 2-3 years to break compaction, otherwise rotary. No-till for maize into wheat stubble.
